subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: Should OpenClaw guarantee that credentials used by approved tools are inaccessible to the general agent shell through a core capability broker, or formally retain the current shared host-process trust boundary?
rationale: The guarantee determines process isolation, plugin APIs, configuration and migration contracts, and whether arbitrary host exec can remain enabled; implementation cannot safely choose this boundary on its own.

options.title: Create a core credential broker
options.body: Add capability-scoped dispatch and plugin-provider APIs so approved operations receive credentials without exposing raw values to the general agent process.

options.title: Use plugin-managed isolation
options.body: Keep core SecretRefs as configuration indirection and document supported plugin or OS-isolation patterns for stronger credential separation.

options.title: Retain the shared trust boundary
options.body: Document that agents with arbitrary host exec share the credential trust domain and focus core work on warnings, least privilege, and redaction.

recommendation.title: Create a core credential broker
recommendation.body: Add capability-scoped dispatch and plugin-provider APIs so approved operations receive credentials without exposing raw values to the general agent process.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the latest explicit security assessment and are the clearest available owner for choosing whether this guarantee belongs in core.
